subject: Architecture
title: Desert Architecture: Thriving in Extreme Heat
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Desert Architecture: Thriving in Extreme Heat.

hook.text: Temperatures in Gulf cities reach 130°F. Architects are designing buildings that create their own cool climates.

buildup.text: Traditional courtyard houses used thick walls and wind towers — 'badgirs' — to cool rooms without electricity.

discovery.text: Modern architects are reviving these ideas — combining passive cooling with smart glass and thermal mass.

twist.text: Qatar cooled outdoor World Cup stadiums to 68°F in desert heat — using solar-powered air conditioning systems.

climax.text: Desert regions will house billions by 2100. Architecture must make extreme heat livable without melting the planet.

punchline.text: Ancient wind towers worked for centuries. Now we're remembering why.

quiz.question: What are 'badgirs' in traditional desert architecture?
options: Wind towers that cool rooms without electricity
Thick mud walls that block sandstorms
